# Spec to code with a model: does a Phrase spec get verified-correct code more reliably
<!-- GENERATED from the Phrase Board (issue #107, sha256:2c281f8cddb2b1bd30f3e58e2a094d896e8be57d5a87ae2e78577914d957e0fd). Do not edit this file: edit the issue. -->


- **Status:** Ready
- **Shape:** Story
- **Type:** data (thin slice; an experiment, no frozen number until a Decider sets it before any row)
- **Milestone:** Tests first: spec to test is the reliable artifact
- **Source:** Product direction, 2026-10-27 (keep Phrase's own deterministic compilers; test-code generation first, then implementation code; the LLM-as-compiler path is a hypothesis measured alongside, not instead) and Decider D74 (Codex, Copilot, Grok Support-it). The measure-first cards (102, 103) stay ahead of these.
- **Depends on:** 106
- **Story:** As Steve, I want a cold model to write C# from the Phrase spec of orders.phrase and from the same behaviour as a plain-English spec, with the generated specs judging both, so that I learn whether a testable spec makes model-written code more reliably correct.
- **Acceptance criteria (Given/When/Then; at most 3, each failing on partial work):**
  1. Given a Decider that fixes, BEFORE any row, the arms (Phrase spec, plain-English spec of the same behaviour), N, the models, the attempt cap, the judge (the same generated xUnit specs for both arms) and what counts as better, When the run finishes, Then each row records pass, attempts, tokens in and out, arm, cold, and proof level specs-passed (the check fails if the Decider is missing or dated after the first row)
  2. Given the plain-English arm, When its prompt is written, Then it states exactly the behaviour of the Phrase spec with no extra hints, a non-author reviews its fairness, and a test asserts neither prompt contains the other arm's syntax or any generated test code
  3. Given the stored rows, When summarized, Then pass rate, attempts and tokens per arm and model are shown without a verdict beyond what the Decider pre-registered

## Context

- Measured ALONGSIDE the compilers, never instead (the product owner's ruling). Context: spec-driven tools mostly treat specs as prompts with no guarantee; a spec that deterministically becomes tests is the gap this card measures.
- Safety rules apply in full; cold runs, tracked background task, finite allotments paced.
